newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS TEAM "DISAPPOINTED" OVER SENNA CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS TEAM "DISAPPOINTED" OVER SENNA CHARGES.

text.p: Britain's Williams Formula One
motor racing team on Monday expressed disappointment at the news
from Italy that team boss Frank Williams will be charged for
manslaughter over the death of Brazilian driver Ayrton Senna.
A statement issued by the team read: "Williams Grand Prix
engineering is disappointed at the content of the summons
requesting that Frank Williams, chief executive, Patrick Head,
technical director, and Adrian Newey, chief designer, appear
before the magistrate at Imola on 20th February 1997 to answer
charges arising from the accident that caused the death of
Ayrton Senna at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix.
"We do not believe that the charges are well founded and
intend to do all that is necessary to defend our position and
contest the charges."
Williams' Italian lawyer Roberto Causo said the hearing had
been set for February 20 before a local judge in Imola, where
Senna was killed in a crash during the San Marino Grand Prix on
Although Frank Williams himself has maintained a dignified
silence since Senna's death, he did suggest in an interview with
the British motor racing magazine Autosport earlier this year
that he may welcome the opportunity to defend himself in court.
"In a way, it will be worse if the magistrate says he thinks
we are culpable and have a case to answer and the judge then
decides not to go ahead with any prosecution," he was quoted.
"If there's a statement from the magistrates saying one
thing and we then don't have the opportunity to defend our
position that would be a bad situation."
The trial leaves the future of Formula One in Italy in
question, especially following recent comments from Benetton
team boss Flavio Briatore, one of the most important men in the
sport, that he would be unwilling to race in Italy if Williams
was convicted.
"If anyone were to be convicted in Italy, it would be big
trouble," he said at the Bologna motor show. "I would not risk
bringing my team to a country that can convict you for an
accident. Fatality is part of the game."
